scores.claim_text: In 2021, StandardAero received a major new platform award for the J85 engine from the U.S. Air Force (USAF) and stood up a dedicated team at its San Antonio facility, achieving USAF 'Gold' rated J85 test cells.
scores.M_value: RECURRING_FEDERAL; 21 UEIs resolved incl. STANDARD AERO (SAN ANTONIO) INC. Top DoD awards include 'J85 DEPOT MAINTENANCE' $73.2M (FA812422F0030), 'J85 MRO' $38.3M (FA812424F0020), plus T56 awards. 179 DoD awards.
scores.interpretation: USAspending affirmatively corroborates the USAF J85 platform award: named San Antonio entity holds multiple USAF J85 depot/MRO contracts (Air Force base symbol FA8124). Registry confirms exactly the claimed program at the claimed facility. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Approximately $895 million, or 19.6%, of StandardAero's 2023 revenue was derived from contracts, directly or indirectly, with the U.S. military.
scores.M_value: contracts_amount_M = $977.6M aggregate federal; 179 Department of Defense awards; signal RECURRING_FEDERAL. Direct DoD awards alone (J85, T56 depot MRO at San Antonio) are tens of millions each.
scores.interpretation: Registry confirms a large, recurring DoD prime-contract footprint consistent with a material (~$895M, 19.6%) U.S. military revenue line. The disclosure correctly notes much of the military revenue is INDIRECT (subcontract) which USAspending under-captures, yet even visible prime awards are substantial. No underdelivery — the federal registry corroborates a material military relationship. PASS.

scores.claim_text: StandardAero is the only independent service provider in North America officially authorized to service a number of platforms including the Rolls-Royce AE 1107 and AE 2100 (military engines powering the V-22 Osprey and C-130J).
scores.M_value: StandardAero federal presence = RECURRING_FEDERAL with 179 DoD military-engine MRO awards (J85, T56 depot overhaul at San Antonio). RTX/P&W 10-K/20-F counterparty mention of 'StandardAero' = 0 hits (expected: AE 1107/AE 2100 are Rolls-Royce engines, not P&W; and OEMs rarely name their authorized MRO shops).
scores.interpretation: The broader claim — that StandardAero is an authorized, contracted military-engine MRO provider — is corroborated by the heavy DoD MRO contract base. The specific AE 1107/AE 2100 (Rolls-Royce) authorization is not separately registry-recorded; counterparty-disclosure absence is non-informative per Heuristic 5 (P&W is the wrong OEM; OEMs do not separately disclose authorized service shops). The verifiable core (military engine MRO authorization + contracts) holds. PASS.

scores.claim_text: On August 23, 2024, StandardAero acquired Aero Turbine Inc., adding source approval request (SAR) capabilities on strategic military platforms; Aero Turbine generated revenues and net income of $70.1M and $14.3M for FY2023.
scores.M_value: RECURRING_FEDERAL; AERO TURBINE, INC (UEI LUMJB673C9K9); 25 DoD awards; top awards all 'J85 MISTR OVERHAUL COMPONENTS' — $87.7M (FA812224F0053), $49.7M, $43.3M (Air Force base symbol FA8122).
scores.interpretation: USAspending affirmatively corroborates the Aero Turbine 'SAR capabilities on strategic military platforms' claim: Aero Turbine is a recurring USAF prime for J85 MISTR (Management of Items Subject To Repair) component overhaul. The military-platform SAR characterization is independently verified, and the ~$70M revenue figure is plausible against the multi-year DoD award stream. PASS.

scores.claim_text: In March 2023 StandardAero became the first and only independent aftermarket provider in North America to join CFM's authorized service network for LEAP-1A/-1B via a CFM Branded Service Agreement (CBSA); one of only five total CBSA holders in the world.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts StandardAero @ GE/CFM CIK 0000040545; edgar_fts StandardAero all-filers
scores.M_value: GE direct-CIK mention of 'StandardAero' = 0 hits. All-filer EDGAR full-text = 156 hits across Woodward, Polaris, Audax Credit BDC and other filers — entity is real and widely referenced, but no filing independently confirms the CFM LEAP CBSA award specifically.
scores.interpretation: The CBSA is a private commercial OEM-authorization agreement that no federal registry records and that CFM/GE do not separately disclose in SEC filings (counterparty-disclosure absence is non-informative per Heuristic 5). Broad external validation of the company exists (156 filer mentions), but the distinctive 'one of only five CBSA holders / only Americas independent' claim cannot be independently confirmed. Marked MODERATE (partial corroboration: real company, plausible but registry-unconfirmable distinctive award), not SEVERE — no registry contradicts it and the surrounding military MRO footprint is verified.

scores.claim_text: As of June 30, 2024 StandardAero holds OEM licenses/authorizations on over 40 key engine platforms from every major OEM including GE Aerospace, CFM, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Honeywell and Safran.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts StandardAero @ GE CIK 0000040545 and RTX/P&W CIK 0000101829; all-filer full-text
scores.M_value: GE = 0 hits; RTX/P&W = 0 hits for 'StandardAero'. All-filer = 156 hits (real entity). USAspending separately confirms GE/Honeywell/Rolls-Royce-platform military MRO (J85=GE, T56=Rolls-Royce/Allison, AE-series=Rolls-Royce) via 179 DoD awards.
scores.interpretation: OEM authorization licenses are private contractual instruments; named OEMs do not enumerate their authorized MRO licensees in SEC filings, so 0 counterparty hits is non-informative (Heuristic 5). Indirect corroboration is strong: the DoD MRO award stream confirms StandardAero overhauls multiple OEMs' military engines (GE J85, Rolls-Royce/Allison T56 and AE series). The specific '40+ platforms across all six named OEMs' headcount is not separately registry-verifiable. MODERATE — partial/indirect corroboration; no contradiction.

scores.claim_text: StandardAero relies on proprietary technology, intellectual property, predictive-analytics models and trade secrets in its aftermarket services business.
scores.interpretation: Zero granted patents — but this is NOT the Nikola pattern (Heuristic 7). StandardAero never claims a patent portfolio; its IP disclosure is explicitly trade-secret / proprietary-method / OEM-licensed-know-how based (an MRO services business, not a product/patent company). Trade secrets and OEM-license know-how are by definition not in USPTO. Absence of patents is fully consistent with the disclosure, so no severity is warranted. UNVERIFIABLE (no registry covers trade-secret IP), not SEVERE.
